drhp.business: Current Infraprojects is an EPC contractor that began with localised electrical and civil works in Rajasthan and has expanded into water infrastructure, specialised MEP services, railway electrification and Solar EPC. It also runs an in-house NABL-accredited testing laboratory and, through wholly-owned SPVs, owns and operates RESCO solar plants that sell power under long-term Power Purchase Agreements to institutional, commercial and industrial customers.
drhp.end_markets: Rajasthan|Kerala|Tamil Nadu|Maharashtra|Karnataka|Utilities/Discoms (B2G)|Private and infrastructure sector (B2B)|Public and institutional clients
drhp.expansion: Current Infraprojects has incorporated four wholly-owned Special Purpose Vehicles (Current Infra Bolnada Solar, Current Infra Talabera Solar, Current Infra Ompura Solar, Current Infra Dhanbad Solar) to build a RESCO platform that develops, owns and operates renewable-energy assets under long-term Power Purchase Agreements. All four SPVs were commissioned during FY26, their operational debut, contributing a combined 9.4 MW of solar capacity across four plants on 25-year PPAs (with a five-year extension option); FY27 is expected to be the first full year of generation. On the EPC side, the company commissioned a 7.52 MWp on-grid solar plant under PM-KUSUM Component C, a 585.6 kW grid-connected rooftop plant for THDC India, a 1.8 MW solar plant at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, and 3 MW+ of solar plants across railway stations in Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka. It is evaluating roughly ₹200 crore of Solar and Solar+BESS tenders, and continues geographic expansion into Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Karnataka beyond its Rajasthan base, alongside continued investment in technology, equipment and project-execution capability.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- India's grid-connected rooftop solar capacity and cumulative solar capacity are expanding, with continued policy support through programmes such as PM-Surya Ghar and the MNRE grid-connected rooftop solar programme, widening the Solar EPC opportunity beyond large utility-scale projects into commercial, industrial, institutional and residential applications.
- Government investment in grid strengthening and power distribution infrastructure (RDSS-scheme mandates) is driving demand for the core Electrical Infrastructure & Utilities business.
- Segment mix is shifting: Solar EPC scaled sharply in FY26 (largest revenue contributor), while the order book shows a more balanced mix across Electrical EPC, Solar EPC and Water EPC than FY26 execution reflected.
- Geographic concentration in FY26 execution (Rajasthan) is expected to broaden, with the order book already showing a larger Kerala and other-states share than FY26 revenue.
- Customer mix is shifting from a B2B-dominated revenue base toward greater B2G participation in the order book, anchored by RDSS-scheme mandates from Jaipur and Jodhpur Discoms.
- RDSS-funded contracts, backed directly by the Central Government, carry a materially shorter payment cycle than typical state-DISCOM contracts, reducing working-capital drag relative to industry peers.
- Geopolitical developments contributed to volatility in raw-material and logistics costs during FY26, moderating EBITDA margin from the prior year's elevated levels despite overall margin resilience.
- Order book stood at ₹305 crore at 31 March 2026, equivalent to about 1.9x FY26 revenue, providing execution visibility into FY27.
- Order book expanded roughly 2.5x between FY23 and FY26.
- Order book segment mix is more balanced than FY26 revenue: Electrical EPC 54%, Solar EPC 28%, Water EPC 16%, versus FY26 revenue mix of Solar EPC 62%, Electrical EPC 20%, Water EPC 9%.
- Order book geographic mix: Rajasthan 52%, Kerala 36%, other states 12%, versus FY26 revenue concentration of Rajasthan 78%.
- Order book customer mix: B2B 65%, B2G 35%, versus FY26 revenue mix of B2B 86%, B2G 14%.
- Order book includes a ₹10.30 crore JVVNL order dated 11 May 2026.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: Current Infraprojects has incorporated four wholly-owned Special Purpose Vehicles (Current Infra Bolnada Solar, Current Infra Talabera Solar, Current Infra Ompura Solar, Current Infra Dhanbad Solar) to build a RESCO platform that develops, owns and operates renewable-energy assets under long-term Power Purchase Agreements. All four SPVs were commissioned during FY26, their operational debut, contributing a combined 9.4 MW of solar capacity across four plants on 25-year PPAs (with a five-year extension option); FY27 is expected to be the first full year of generation. On the EPC side, the company commissioned a 7.52 MWp on-grid solar plant under PM-KUSUM Component C, a 585.6 kW grid-connected rooftop plant for THDC India, a 1.8 MW solar plant at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, and 3 MW+ of solar plants across railway stations in Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Karnataka. It is evaluating roughly ₹200 crore of Solar and Solar+BESS tenders, and continues geographic expansion into Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Karnataka beyond its Rajasthan base, alongside continued investment in technology, equipment and project-execution capability.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- integration: In-house NABL-accredited MEC Test Lab brings quality testing and control in-house, strengthening execution capabilities — evidence: NABL-accredited in-house testing lab with 48 to 72 hour testing turnaround.
- customer lock-in: RESCO platform generates contracted, non-cyclical income independent of tender cycles — evidence: 25-year Power Purchase Agreements on four commissioned RESCO solar plants (9.4 MW), generating over ₹6 crore of annual recurring revenue.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Steel, aluminium, cables and equipment drive project cost; commodity spikes or supply shocks squeeze margins where escalation cannot be passed through.
- Shortages or late delivery of modules, transformers and cables delay schedules and raise costs.
- Approval, land, right-of-way or utility delays defer execution and revenue while overheads continue.
- Aggressive bids or delayed awards hit intake and margins; reliance on a few significant customers adds exposure to their buying plans.
- Solar and RESCO projects hinge on approvals, grid connectivity, PPA execution, commissioning and counterparty payments; policy shifts can alter project economics.
- Dependencies across engineering, procurement, subcontractors, labour and site work; delays or poor resource use cause overruns.
- Costs are paid upfront while collections follow milestones; any mismatch raises working-capital needs.
- Rapid order growth and new geographies stretch management bandwidth, skilled manpower and systems.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversify into complementary engines of growth rather than simply adding businesses — building Solar EPC and RESCO alongside the core Electrical Infrastructure & Utilities franchise.
- Build a recurring-revenue layer through the RESCO platform (owned solar assets under long-term PPAs) to reduce dependence on project-based, cyclical EPC tendering.
- Grow with capital discipline: remain selective in project participation, manage working capital closely, and allocate capital toward opportunities that generate sustainable returns.
- Expand geographically beyond the Rajasthan anchor market into Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu, sharing equipment and engineering resources across high-density execution hubs.
- Strengthen execution as a scalable capability (project monitoring, procurement planning, resource utilisation, working-capital management, digital project management systems) rather than a project-level strength.
- Evaluate RESCO-BESS and integrated energy/storage solutions to expand participation in the renewable-energy ecosystem.
